about: The thumb of the shape study's hand model, before and after the corrections of the research redo (RA, 2026-11-09). Only the thumb changes; the fingers, the two placements, the contact band (y 15) and the sizes are the model's. Three "after" blocks, one per value of the thumb's knuckle at rest (Brock chooses).
shape: each block: hand (as export_deck.py writes GD.hand), slide and path (as longarcs.py writes them to out/longarcs.json), thumb_by_hand (the table of the report)
frame: the mouse's, mm: z toward the nose from the footprint's middle, height above the pad. The thumb touches the side at the contact band's middle, height 15 mm, in both placements (the model's rule).

why.THUMB_BONES: Links between joint centres. Base to knuckle 37 mm: 38.6 in one specimen of 203 mm (Goislard de Monsabert et al. 2018, ESM Table S3) and 35.9 in the open MyoHand model; the whole first bone is 46.2 mm (SD 3.9) between its joint surfaces (Buryanov & Kotiuk 2010, Table I; 48.6 scaled), but the base joint turns about a point inside the bone's near end. Knuckle to tip joint 35: Buryanov's 31.57 x 1.052 + about 2. Tip joint to the bone's tip 26: 21.67 x 1.052 + about 3. The chain ends at the bone's tip, as the fingers' chains do; the skin's tip is 6 mm further (5.67 x 1.052) and the pad's centre about 3 mm nearer. Status: two sources for the first link, the others derived.
why.THUMB_CMC_BACK: The base's centre 56 mm behind the index knuckle's for the mean hand: 56.0 mm in the specimen (hand 203 mm, so 53.3 scaled), 58.0 mm in MyoHand (a hand of about 185 to 190 mm). Range 0.275 to 0.34 hand lengths.
why.THUMB_CMC_PALMAR: 11.5 mm under the knuckle line: the specimen 9.9, MyoHand 13.1. The model's 10 was an estimate.
why.tip_joint_10: Measured: Lee & Jung 2014, 10 deg (SD 6), 40 hands, skin markers; Rogers et al. 2008, 100 hands, landmarks on the palm side: 6 deg (SD 15) relaxed round a large ball, 17 deg (SD 16) holding a mouse.
why.knuckle_39: Measured: Lee & Jung 2014, 39 deg (SD 12), 40 relaxed hands, forearm neutral, skin markers; the paper does not define what the angle is measured from.
why.knuckle_25: An estimate: 39 less a marker over-read of 6 to 24 deg, so 15 to 33 deg, taken at about the middle. The over-read: markers on the skin stand at different heights above the bones' axes (about 14 mm at the thumb's knuckle, 12 mm at its tip joint, marker centres included; the height of the base's "virtual" marker is not given: 0 if at the joint's centre, 12 if at the skin), so a straight thumb reads 6 to 24 deg bent across links of 37 and 35 mm. For fingers the same kind of markers read 4 to 5 deg high against a goniometer at about 30 deg (Cook et al. 2007, J Appl Biomech 23:70-78, 5 people).
why.knuckle_12_5: Described, not measured: Cooney, Lucca, Chao & Linscheid 1981 (J Bone Joint Surg 63-A:1371-81) describe their rest position as the thumb against the side of the index's end bone with the knuckle and tip joint each flexed 10 to 15 deg.

This moves the little finger about 3.8 mm toward the tail in both placements and so lengthens the overlap. Not part of the thumb variant; offered for the rerun.
